Many youths in XX have limited powers and freedom because they are under the authority of their parents.
A large number of youths in XX do not have plots to grow their own crops. About 25% of youths have plots to grow crops of their choice but the plots are small.
We have power and freedom to approach a girl of my choice but long ago it was difficult.
Some youth have powers and freedom to do whatever they want to do because they are just wayward.
We are free to go to a church of our choice.
Among the youths that go to church there are some who are limited in doing many things they want because church doctrines do not allow that.
Education is very important because you always have something [gainful] to do in life.
Education equips us with knowledge of doing something [gainful] in life.
Education allows us to have better life and gives us dignity in the community.
Education trains us to have discipline in most of the things we do in life.
With education you can marry a successful woman.
All: The majority of boys end schooling at Form 4.
[And girls?] All: The majority of girls end schooling at Form 1 and 2.
Boys must learn until they die because they are the ones that have the responsibility to support their families.
Girls must learn up to university level.
For girls it depends with their behavior.
Parents show same commitment to educating their daughters as their sons depending on the behavior of the child.
If there is inadequate money, the parent will pay for the boy child. They say he shall be the household head.

Other parents pay for the brighter child, whether girl or boy, if there is inadequate money. If it is the boy who is not bright then he has no choice but to start doing no-tillage planting basin CA. [laughter from the floor]

ALL [one after the other]: If it is the girl who is not bright then she goes for a driving course [laughter]. She will be driving on the house floor. Who will buy her undies if she does not do that? She cannot move without undies [laughter continues].
We are just forced to do agriculture by our parents. There is no benefit for us as youths to do agriculture.

[Do others think the same?] It is not about perceptions. It is the reality. There is no benefit for us in farming. We do all the hard work but when the crop is harvested and sold, only the parents get the money. They do not include us in their plans.
They should leave us to concentrate on our books. I can take my books with me when I go to herd cattle.

[Alright, you do agriculture against your will, but what agricultural activities do you learn about anyway?] Agricultural activities that we learn are ploughing the field using an ox-drawn plough, weeding the crops, spraying the crops, harvesting the crops, milking cows and herding cattle.
We learn most of agricultural activities practically during everyday practice.

Conservation agriculture
It conserves soil moisture and there is efficient use of manure since we apply it directly per plant station.
New improved varieties of maize
Most people are growing SC513 while a few people have adopted Pioneer 2859.
Most people prefer SC513 because it is not easily attacked by pests and diseases. If planted in good soil it gives high yields.
The area put under maize in XX is declining because of labor shortages. The quantity of maize harvested is also declining since the area under maize production is declining.
75% of people in the community are growing maize.

The amount of rainfall we are receiving is decreasing but last year there was much more rainfall as compared to the last ten years. Among all the maize farmers in XX, 25% have adopted Pioneer seed varieties which are drought tolerant. Women prefer SC401 because is a very early maturity variety and men prefer SC513 because it gives high yields.
Forest conservation
It assists in conserving the soil and provides pasture for our livestock. Trees are important because they produce oxygen which we breathe.
New improved varieties

We are ranking new improved varieties at number two because they give us high yields, they are drought resistance, have good germination percentage and they are not easily affected by pest and diseases.
And which have been most important for the [women]? Why? [Please rank the top 2 in order of importance for each sex, and be sure to get explanations for the ratings.]
Forest conservation
They easily get firewood near their homesteads.
They are able to get thatching grass for their houses.
New improved varieties
They are important for the same reasons as for the men; they give high yields, are drought tolerant, have good germination percentage and they are not easily affected by pest and diseases.

We have different opportunities because as we grow we are told that girls’ work is in the house while boys work is in the fields. Because of those traditional norms boys have a better opportunity than girls to learn about and try out new farming practices.

In 2004, the amount of rainfall we received did not allow us to grow maize. As result of inadequate rainfall, we grew sorghum [which is drought tolerant]. We have moved to maize because growing sorghum is labor intensive.
Donkeys were important in 2004 because our cattle were unable to provide draught power because of drought. Pigs and sheep are not very important to us.
Cattle and donkeys are important because they assist us with draught power.

We are following the customs of women doing certain agricultural activities and men doing others. Women are doing all domestic chores and growing of groundnuts, cowpeas and roundnuts while men do all agricultural activities and are trained to do craft work. We are following this because when a girl is married she will be responsible for keeping the family while the men will be working for the family.
It is rare in this community for a young woman to do farming activities that are supposed to be done by young men. It is difficult for a young woman to grow maize or rear cattle.

It is rare for young men and boys in XX to grow groundnuts, roundnuts and cowpeas. People will laugh at him because he will do the activities which are supposed to be done by women. Other young men and boys in the community will think that the young man trying to grow crops associated with young women is mad.
In polygamous families, each and every wife has her own plot.
In non-polygamous families, they have plots for the family. Women will be given a plot to grow groundnuts, cowpeas and roundnuts.
We consider the type of soil in the plot; maize is put on plots with heavy soils. We also consider the size of the plots.
Men in this community do not work on their wives’ plots. A few will only assist their wives in ploughing the fields.
Women frequently work in their husbands’ plots because that is where the food for the family is produced. They work in the man’s plot from preparing the field up to harvesting of the crop.
In this community farmers are organized into groups headed by a lead farmer. Thus, if there are additional labour requirements, men invite other members of the collective work group.
They hire additional labor from people within the community and pay with either maize grain or money.
Working in town and gold panning.
[In general, is the right kind of labor available for agricultural activities when needed?] Most people in the community have inadequate labor for their farming activities.
[How do [men] obtain additional labor when needed - in or outside the household?] They invite other members of the collective work group.
They hire additional labor from people within the community and pay with either maize grain or money.
How do female-headed households go about obtaining adult male labor when they need it during the rainy season?]
They hire additional labor from men in the community and pay with either maize grain or money.
Some women are able to do those activities that are done by men.
She consults her husband.
And would a man consult someone first before planting a new crop? If so, who? [Again, inquire if he would consult his wife if this is not mentioned.]
He consults his wife.
He does not consult anyone, he just tells his family that we are going to grow this crop this season in this plot. No one will oppose the father’s idea.
Adam will not allow Ana to join a local group because the opportunities of selling the vegetables and controlling the income will be limited.
Adam will be angry about Ana’s decision to sell her vegetables. The end result will be a conflict between Adam and Ana.
Adam will agree with Ana’s idea but take all the money from the sale of the vegetables.
Adam will not ask Ana for less help on his plots; Ana will first work in Adam’s plot.
Adam will hire additional labor and pay with money from the sale of vegetables.
Some people in the community will think that Mary gave Mark love potion.
Some people admire Mary because she is working for the family.
We tell Mark the truth that he has been given love potion by Mary.
If we tell Mark to refuse doing house work, during the night Mark will be denied sex by Mary.
If there are no conflicts in their house because of the ‘reversed’ roles, it means the two understand each other. We will therefore encourage Mark to keep on doing what he is doing.
Mark will be happy and start to work hard within the house.
Mark will think Mary is doing other things [prostitution] at the market rather than selling vegetables.
Mark will decide to accompany Mary to the market to investigate whether all the money is coming from the sale of vegetables.
Gender equality is bad because women will see themselves as people having same power with their husbands. It means having equal opportunity at work but not in home as other women are doing.
Gender equality is good because some men were oppressing their wives. Its main purpose was to give each and every person his /her rights.
It is not good for a woman to have equal powers as the man. The powers of men are now limited.
We should not have same powers; men should have more powers than women. A woman is there to help me in whatever I do in my life. We should only have equal powers at work, not in the home.
David and Diana are a couple that work together in all their agricultural activities. They jointly make all decisions about their family and life together.

It depends on who is working most in the garden. Diana will sell the vegetables, if she is the one who is working most in the garden and David will sell the vegetables if he is the one who is working most in the garden.
If there is fertilizer, David will try to plant the new variety.
If Diana tells David about the new variety with humility and respect, David will welcome the idea.
